mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% year-over-year indicates inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY > 2% and S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the cases.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and subsequent monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE < 4% and S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong consumer demand, which boosts economic growth and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases and S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a slowdown in economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO decreases and S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the cases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) combined with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, which can lead to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases, but S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS decreases and S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the cases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS increases and S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the cases.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in GDP (GDPC1) indicates strong economic growth, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 increases and S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the cases.
